newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-TOULOUSE AND BRIVE AIM FOR ALL-FRENCH FINAL.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TOULOUSE AND BRIVE AIM FOR ALL-FRENCH FINAL.

text.p: Holders Toulouse, badly stung by Wasps when they last played in England, will be looking to reassert the status of French club rugby at Leicester in their European Cup semifinal on Saturday.

Leicester's Australian coach Bob Dwyer, however, has no doubts as to the task facing his team. Despite Wasps' 77-17 win over Toulouse in the group stage, he regards the French champions as "the best team in Europe".
Guy Noves, one of Toulouse's two coaches, said: "The scar will be healed if we put on a very great performance at Leicester."

Toulouse hope to spoil Leicester's Twickenham final plans with a victory that would pit them either against Cardiff in a repeat of last year's final or Brive in an all-French decider which would wrest the January 25 final from the English Rugby Football Union headquarters.
Brive are at home to Cardiff on Sunday in the second of the semifinals in which freezing weather conditions are playing a major part.
Leicester have practised 160 kms from home on an indoor pitch at Worcester while their Welford Road ground is covered to protect it from the ravages of the cold snap.

Brive, too, have trained indoors on a handball court and their pitch is covered with 25 tonnes of straw sandwiched between two sheets of plastic which soldiers from the local garrison will help the club to remove at midday on Sunday.

Toulouse will have to control Dean Richards and his troops in the Leicester pack on Saturday before they can launch their superior backs at the suspect English defence -- if the weather allows for open play.

Toulouse will be at full strength with wing and captain Emile N'Tamack and centre Thomas Castaignede, who missed the two-test series France lost to South Africa last month through injury, both back in the side.
Castaignede, who has been nursing a damaged rib, will wear a protective corset.
"Physical combat is going to prevail over technical qualities," said the talented centre, who fears the weather conditions will favour the Leicester pack which he regards as the best in Europe.
Leicester will be without their giant young Irish back row forward Eric Miller, who preferred to turn out for his country against Italy with a view to securing a place in Ireland's Five Nations side.
Dwyer, who as Australia's 1991 World Cup-winning coach was one of those responsible for creating southern hemisphere superiority in the game, makes no secret of his regard for the European Cup.
"This European Cup is a hugely important event," he told a British newspaper.

"This tournament has the potential to really go places. Remember the Super 12 wasn't all that hot when it started out only a few years back... It won't be long before we have a world club championship."
Brive v Cardiff should provide an appetising duel of fly-halves with captain Alain Penaud, just back from an ankle injury, pitting his wits against Wales veteran Jonathan Davies.
Penaud said: "The key is to vary our game. We have to disorientate them. I believe if we manage to put them out of position, to impose a furious rhythm, we can annul their strength."
Cardiff, who showed glaring weaknesses in some departments in a surprise home defeat by Pontypridd last Saturday, must recover the form of their fine quarter-final victory over Bath.
An unusually ponderous Davies fell foul of a fast Pontypridd back row, while the Cardiff forwards were outplayed in the line-outs, usually one of their strengths.
Cardiff will be without Wales prop David Young, who injured his shoulder during last month's test against the Springboks.
But flanker Gwyn Jones is back after six months out with a shoulder injury and captain Hemi Taylor also returns after recovering from a shoulder injury.
